first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding addresses both the 4% completion decline and likely part of the 6% activation decline without introducing discount-driven retention or account-quality risk. Verify memory_86 because its evidence stops at early adoption, not sustainable qualified revenue, and memory_73 because promotional pricing directly addresses the competitive threat but may have unresolved downstream quality, margin, or retention effects. Current intent remains provisional pending those records.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified record shows completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable value. Promotional pricing is rejected because its +18% qualified-revenue lift was offset by 30-day retention falling 12% and failure at first renewal. Longer-term revenue impact beyond the observed retention window remains uncertain, so guardrails should include qualified activation, retention, and expansion signals.
